subject: english-language
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Paper 1: assessment structure and assessment objectives

questions.q: What percentage of the overall GCSE grade is Paper 1: Fiction and Imaginative Writing worth?
questions.explain: Paper 1 is worth 40% of the Edexcel GCSE English Language qualification (Paper 2 carries the remaining 60%).

questions.q: How long is the Paper 1 examination?
questions.explain: Paper 1 is a written examination lasting 1 hour 45 minutes, covering both the reading and writing sections.

questions.q: The Section A reading extract is always taken from fiction of which period?
questions.explain: Section A of Paper 1 assesses an extract from 19th-century fiction.

questions.q: How is the Section A fiction extract best described in terms of student preparation?
options: Studied in advance as a set text
questions.explain: Students respond to an unseen 19th-century fiction extract that they have not studied beforehand.

questions.q: What does Assessment Objective 1 (AO1) mainly require students to do?
options: Identify and interpret explicit and implicit information and ideas
Analyse how writers use language and structure
questions.explain: AO1 assesses the ability to identify and interpret explicit and implicit information and ideas in a text.

questions.q: Assessment Objective 2 (AO2) asks students to comment on and analyse how writers use what, supported by subject terminology?
questions.explain: AO2 requires analysis of how writers use language and structure to achieve effects, using appropriate subject terminology.

questions.q: Which assessment objective focuses on evaluating a text critically and supporting the response with textual references?
questions.explain: AO4 assesses critical evaluation of texts, supported by relevant textual references.

questions.q: What type of writing is assessed in Section B of Paper 1?
questions.explain: Section B of Paper 1 assesses imaginative (creative) writing.

questions.q: In Section B, how many writing tasks does a student actually complete?
options: One task chosen from two options
questions.explain: Students choose and complete one imaginative writing task from a choice of two.

questions.q: Which two assessment objectives are used to mark the imaginative writing task?
questions.explain: Writing is assessed through AO5 (content and organisation) and AO6 (technical accuracy).

questions.q: AO5 in the writing task mainly rewards a student's ability to do what?
options: Communicate clearly and imaginatively and organise ideas effectively
questions.explain: AO5 assesses clear, effective and imaginative communication and the organisation of information and ideas.

questions.q: AO6 in the writing task focuses on which aspect of a student's work?
options: Accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar with a range of vocabulary and sentence structures
questions.explain: AO6 rewards technical accuracy in spelling, punctuation and grammar and a range of vocabulary and sentence structures.

questions.q: The imaginative writing prompts in Section B are often accompanied by what stimulus?
questions.explain: Section B writing tasks are frequently supported by a visual image to stimulate imaginative responses.

questions.q: Because Section A gives students only a single extract, which assessment objective is NOT assessed in Paper 1?
questions.explain: AO3 requires comparison of ideas across two texts, so it cannot be assessed on a single-extract paper.

questions.q: A student writes: 'The writer's simile "like a caged beast" suggests the character feels trapped.' Which assessment objective does this best demonstrate?
questions.explain: Analysing a language technique such as a simile and its effect addresses AO2.

questions.q: Which is the most effective way to open an imaginative piece so that it engages the reader immediately?
options: Begin with vivid description or dramatic action
List every event that will happen
State the title and word count
questions.explain: Opening with vivid description or action (often in medias res) hooks the reader and showcases AO5 skills.

questions.q: A student's story has an imaginative plot but is full of spelling and punctuation errors. Which assessment objective is most weakened?
questions.explain: AO6 assesses technical accuracy, so frequent spelling and punctuation errors reduce the AO6 mark.

questions.q: In AO2, what does the phrase 'subject terminology' refer to?
options: Using accurate literary and linguistic terms such as metaphor and personification
questions.explain: Subject terminology means the correct technical vocabulary for analysis, e.g. metaphor, simile, personification.

questions.q: How does a student access the 19th-century fiction text they must analyse in Section A?
options: It is provided within the exam paper
They select it from a reading list
questions.explain: Paper 1 is a closed-book exam; the unseen extract is printed in the examination paper for students to read on the day.

questions.q: A student wants to make a setting feel vivid by appealing to the five senses. Which technique should they use?
questions.explain: Sensory imagery describes sight, sound, smell, taste and touch to create a vivid setting, strengthening AO5.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Language (1EN0) specification; Paper 1: Fiction and Imaginative Writing
